newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament panel wants to lower voting age.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament panel wants to lower voting age.

text.p: A Kuwaiti parliamentary panel has approved a bill that would reduce the minimum age of eligible voters in elections to 18 years instead of 21, a newspaper reported on Monday.
"Parliament's legal and legislative committee on Sunday approved a draft law to reduce the voting age to 18," the Arab Times reported.
However, the measure requires a majority approval by the 62-seat house and the endorsement of the Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah before it becomes law.
"If passed the bill will increase the voting base in the country by several thousands," said the newspaper.

In the October parliamentary elections about 107,000 Kuwaiti men aged more than 21 years were listed to vote. Of the 720,000 Kuwaitis, women, military personnel, policemen and naturalised Kuwaitis cannot vote.
The committee "refused another (bill) calling to grant the voting right to servicemen," the English-language daily added.
Kuwait is the only Gulf Arab country that has a fully-elected legislature.
